extraction.Name: George Ruff
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent in fee to his 640 acre allotment when it was issued, because he did not want to pay taxes; but was advised by the Indian Agency that, if he did not take care of it, the taxes would be assessed against it, and finally be sold for them; so he accepted the patent
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged three quarters of his allotment to the Federal Land Bank of Omaha, Nebraska, for $1200.00; sold one mortgaged quarter to Mrs. Effie Usher of Martin, South Dakota, for $2000.00 ($500.00 cash, balance promised from inherited land from her mother's estate); Mrs. Usher later sold it to J.C. Dix of Martin, South Dakota, who cleared the mortgage held by the Federal Land Bank of Omaha
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: had gotten behind in taxes, and, in 1922, he mortgaged three quarters of his allotment to the Federal Land Bank of Omaha, Nebraska, for $1200.00, and, in order to pay off the mortgage, in 1925, he sold one of these mortgaged quarters
extraction.Occupation/Income: leases his land and he gets one third of the crop; that this is his only income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; has very poor health, having stomach trouble and is also ruptured; has a wife who has pretty fair health; has two children to support who have good health; deponent does not consider that he got a good deal; has never received any help from the County, State, or the United States Government; affidavit sworn November 26, 1928; reference numbers 2204/2200 noted at bottom | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Shannon County, South Dakota (Pine Ridge area)" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')
